newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Bank of Thailand governor has resigned amid mounting pressure from the baht flotation and a challenge to his performance. Rerngchai Marakanond submitted his resignation to Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya. It is expected to be acknowledged by the cabinet in Chiang Rai province today. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Thailand will request standby credits from the International Monetary Fund to supplement official foreign reserves in a bid to defend the baht, Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya says. A restructuring package from the IMF would also help boost confidence in the Thai economy among investors. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Seni Pramoj, a four-time prime minister and a leader of the Seri Thai (Free Thai) movement, died yesterday. He was 92. He succumbed to chronic pulmonary obstruction and kidney failure and died at a hospital. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- Former finance minister Suthee Singhasaneh has agreed to head a powerful new commission entrusted with the job of looking into the Bank of Thailand's examination and supervision of financial institutions. Finance Permanent Secretary Chatu Mongol Sonakul says the commission is formed at the recommendation of the World Bank. (THE NATION)

- Krungthai Thanakit will be ready to cash promissory notes of depositors of the 16 suspended finance companies from September 1. The 16 firms opened for business yesterday for the first time since the Bank of Thailand ordered them to temporarily suspend operations on June 27. (BUSINESS DAY)
